description: Tier-3 in-place modernization: existing Java 11 code (Kiwiplan MES #1, hard Java-11 EOL Sept 2026) upgrading to Java 21 LTS + Spring Boot 3. This is NOT a cross-language migration — source and target are both Java — so the claim taxonomy captures UPGRADE ACTIONS, not idiom gaps. The dominant, mechanical-but-pervasive break is the jakarta namespace: Spring Boot 3 / Jakarta EE 9+ renamed every javax.* (servlet, persistence, validation, annotation, mail, xml.bind) to jakarta.*. Beyond that: APIs REMOVED between JDK 11 and 21 (Nashorn/javax.script nashorn engine gone in 15, RMI Activation, Applet, several sun.* internals under strong encapsulation); APIs DEPRECATED-for-removal still compiling but risky (finalize(), the Integer(int)/Date(y,m,d) constructors, Runtime.exec(String), the URL(String) constructor, SecurityManager); Spring Boot 2→3 breaking changes (WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter removed → SecurityFilterChain bean, antMatchers → requestMatchers, spring.factories → AutoConfiguration.imports, Hibernate 5→6); third-party MAJOR bumps forced by the above (Hibernate 5→6, Jakarta Validation, Jackson, Lombok, Mockito); and the non-breaking Java 21 LANGUAGE modernizations worth adopting (records, sealed classes, pattern matching for switch/instanceof — final in 21, switch expressions, text blocks, virtual threads, Stream.toList()). Because source AND target are Java, source-execution equivalence IS feasible in principle; the maven-sidecar runs JDK 21, so the modernized Java 21 target compiles and its JUnit suite runs offline, but the framework-level (Spring Boot 3 / jakarta) upgrades cannot be compiled offline (no Spring in the sidecar cache) and are expressed as documented contracts, not stubbed.

claimKinds.label: Invariant
claimKinds.description: Behavioural invariants that MUST be preserved bit-for-bit across the 11→21 upgrade — the business rules a reviewer signs off on. The whole point of a modernization is that behaviour is unchanged, so invariants carry the most weight.

claimKinds.label: javax → jakarta namespace
claimKinds.description: A javax.* import/type that Spring Boot 3 / Jakarta EE 9+ renamed to jakarta.* — javax.persistence.*, javax.servlet.*, javax.validation.*, javax.annotation.* (PostConstruct/PreDestroy), javax.mail.*, javax.xml.bind.*. Mechanical but pervasive; every occurrence must move, and the matching dependency changes major version (e.g. hibernate-core → the jakarta-persistence artifact). Note: some javax.* packages did NOT move (javax.sql, javax.crypto, javax.naming stay) — flag only the ones that did.

claimKinds.label: Removed API usage
claimKinds.description: Use of a JDK API that was REMOVED between Java 11 and Java 21 and will NOT compile/run on 21: the Nashorn JavaScript engine + javax.script 'nashorn' (removed JDK 15), RMI Activation (JDK 17), the Applet API (deprecated for removal, gone), pack200, several com.sun.* / sun.* internals now under strong encapsulation (JEP 403, JDK 17), and Thread.stop/suspend/resume behavior. Each needs a concrete replacement or an SME decision.

fields.name: removed_in
fields.doc: The JDK version that removed it, e.g. 'JDK 15'.

fields.name: replacement
fields.doc: The concrete Java 21 replacement, e.g. 'GraalVM JS / a rules engine' for Nashorn.

claimKinds.label: Deprecated (for-removal) API usage
claimKinds.description: Use of an API that still COMPILES on 21 but is deprecated (often for-removal) and should be replaced during the upgrade: Object.finalize(), the Integer(int)/Long(long)/Double(double) boxing constructors (use valueOf), the Date(year,month,day) constructor (use LocalDate/Calendar), Runtime.exec(String) (use the String[] overload / ProcessBuilder), the URL(String) constructor (use URI.create(..).toURL()), and SecurityManager (deprecated for removal, JEP 411).

claimKinds.label: Spring Boot 2 → 3 upgrade action
claimKinds.description: A Spring Boot 2 → 3 (Spring Framework 6) breaking change: WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter removed → a SecurityFilterChain @Bean; HttpSecurity.antMatchers/mvcMatchers → requestMatchers; spring.factories auto-config → META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports; @ConstructorBinding placement change; trailing-slash matching now off by default; Hibernate 5 → 6 (HQL/Criteria changes, the id-generator default change); and many property renames. Each is an explicit upgrade action tied to the jakarta move (SB3 requires Java 17+ and jakarta).

fields.name: sb3_form
fields.doc: The Spring Boot 3 replacement, e.g. 'a SecurityFilterChain @Bean using requestMatchers'.

claimKinds.label: Third-party library major bump
claimKinds.description: A third-party dependency that must jump a MAJOR version because of the Java 21 / jakarta / Spring Boot 3 move, with its own breaking changes: Hibernate 5 → 6 (jakarta.persistence, new id generation), the Jakarta Validation provider (hibernate-validator 6 → 8), Jackson, Lombok (Java 21 support needs a recent version), Mockito (inline mock maker / JDK 21), and the build plugins (maven-compiler/surefire, spring-boot-maven-plugin 3.x). Flag the library, the from→to majors, and the notable breakage.

claimKinds.label: Java 21 modernization opportunity
claimKinds.description: A NON-breaking chance to adopt a Java 21 language feature that makes the upgraded code clearer and is finalized (no --enable-preview): a verbose data-carrier POJO (getters/equals/hashCode/toString) → a record; a closed type hierarchy → a sealed interface + records; an if-else/instanceof chain → pattern matching for switch (JEP 441, final in 21); a statement switch → a switch expression; concatenated multi-line strings → a text block; a thread-per-request executor → virtual threads (JEP 444); and Stream.collect(toList()) → Stream.toList(). These are opportunities, not requirements — the SME decides scope.

claimKinds.label: Edge case
claimKinds.description: Subtle BEHAVIOURAL changes across 11→21 that a purely mechanical upgrade can miss: strictfp is now always-on (JEP 306, JDK 17) so some floating-point results changed on non-strict code; List.of()/Collectors.toUnmodifiableList() and Stream.toList() return UNMODIFIABLE lists (mutating them throws, unlike the old ArrayList from collect(toList())); the default locale/charset provider and CLDR locale data updated (JDK 9+) so String.format / number formatting can differ; time-zone data updates; and the Hibernate 6 default id-generation / naming-strategy change. Each must be verified, not assumed identical.

claimKinds.label: Open question
claimKinds.description: Upgrade decisions needing SME resolution: whether to adopt the Java Platform Module System (JPMS) or stay on the classpath; which packages need --add-opens because of strong encapsulation (JEP 403) of JDK internals; the replacement strategy for a removed SecurityManager; the build-tool and CI base-image JDK bump (Maven/Gradle plugin versions, Docker base image → temurin:21); and whether to take the virtual-threads throughput win now or defer.

ioFieldShape.directionDescription: Java method/field surfaces. in = parameter; return = return value; field = a class field (relevant when a POJO becomes a record).

promptHints.emphasis: Every javax.* import that moved is a jakartaNamespaceMigration claim (give the exact jakarta.* symbol; do NOT flag javax.sql/crypto/naming which stayed). Removed APIs (Nashorn, RMI Activation, sun.* internals) are removedApiUsage with a concrete replacement. finalize(), boxing constructors, Date(y,m,d), Runtime.exec(String), URL(String), SecurityManager are deprecatedApiUsage. WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter/antMatchers/spring.factories/Hibernate-5 patterns are springBootUpgrade. Hibernate 5→6 and validator/Jackson/Lombok/Mockito bumps are libraryMajorBump. Verbose POJOs, closed hierarchies, instanceof chains, statement switches, multi-line string concatenation are modernizationOpportunity (record/sealed/pattern-switch/switch-expression/text-block). strictfp-always-on, unmodifiable toList(), and locale-data changes are edgeCase. JPMS, --add-opens, and the CI/base-image JDK bump are openQuestions. Behaviour must be preserved — invariants are paramount.

calibratedAgainst: Tier-3 Java 11 portfolio (Kiwiplan MES #1, Java-11 EOL Sept 2026)
JDK 11→21 migration guide + Spring Boot 3.0 migration guide + Jakarta EE 9 rename
